failure_modes: Consistent co‑isolation artifact: orthogonal assays repeatedly detect the same protein/miRNA/particle:protein pattern because non‑vesicular contaminants (e.g., protein aggregates, lipoproteins, or secreted complexes) co-fractionate and are captured by the immuno-capture reagents, so the fingerprint is not EV-specific (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Assay interference / buffer effects: formulation buffers, capture-compatibility reagents, or spike-ins systematically alter recovery or readouts in a way that mimics a lot-specific fingerprint (false positives) or masks real differences (false negatives) across sites (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Limited material / sampling bias: insufficient yield from pilot GMP-like lots forces pooling, heavy subsampling, or limited replicate testing, reducing power to detect lot variability and increasing chance of overfitting a non-generalizable fingerprint (ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Inter‑lab harmonization artifacts: harmonized SOPs, reagents, or centralized data‑processing pipelines introduce correlated biases across sites so that apparent inter‑site concordance reflects shared method bias rather than true robustness (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Biological irrelevance / translation gap: even if the fingerprint is EV‑specific and reproducible in vitro, it may not relate to in vivo delivery or function—e.g., intranasal biodistribution and brain uptake differ by species and formulation, so attributes that look conserved in production may not predict clinical or NHP behavior (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution; ev-zhuang-2011-intranasal-exosome; ev-kodali-2017-status-epilepticus).

False security enabling downstream failures: adopting a non‑numeric fingerprint as a gate could allow lots into bridging/potency studies that later fail functional linkage studies, wasting resources and delaying corrective action (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
strongest_objection: The most bounded, high-impact failure mode is that the proposed composite “intact-EV” fingerprint will appear reproducible across pilot lots and sites while in fact reflecting consistent co‑isolation or assay artifacts (non‑vesicular proteins/lipoproteins, formulation components, or capture reagent interactions) rather than bona fide, membrane‑protected EV signals. Under that scenario the blinded inter‑lab concordance metric will falsely pass, producing a non‑numeric comparability gate that does not track the true EV material or its functional/biological relevance; this risk is amplified by species- and formulation-dependent biodistribution differences that undermine assumptions about what cargo or surface markers are mechanistically meaningful in translational contexts.
